input: In recent quarters, the contract packaging firm, which operates 4 plants and generates revenue of $118 million per year, has experienced a noticeable deterioration in its delivery performance. Based on an analysis of order records covering a period of 12 months and encompassing a total of 13536 orders, on-time delivery over the last two quarters stood at 91%, which falls short of the target of 95%. It is worth noting that Plant 2 accounts for a disproportionate 63% of all late orders across the business. At the same time, overtime cost reached $2.2 million last year, representing an increase of 24% compared with the year before, while the order backlog has grown to some 3.8 weeks, compared with just 1.9 weeks a year ago. A scheduling system covering all plants has been quoted at $260k, whereas Plant 2 alone would cost $112k. An internal estimate — and it should be stressed that this is an internal estimate rather than a vendor figure — suggests that overtime at Plant 2 could potentially be reduced by 15–20% in the first year. The recommendation under consideration is therefore to install the system at Plant 2 first and to hold the other plants until the Plant 2 results are reported, with the operations director owning the scheduling programme, so that the initial commitment is limited to $112k and the plant responsible for 63% of late orders is addressed first; the wider rollout then rests on the Plant 2 evidence.
